item.title: [ZEPPELIN-783] CI: spark download fails the CI on master
item.description:
CI is red on master now for 2 last commits.

Both are the cases when Spark download fails on CI machine, although the symptoms looks similar with ZEPPELIN-776 - those are different issues.

TODO:

  • fail the build if download retries have failed

It looks like there are a few issues here:
1. it seems 2nd retry is leaving behind a partial download file when wget is killed - therefore not allowing the 3rd retry download to start
(see the sequence in 3rd retry:

+cd .spark-dist
+[[ ! -f spark-1.3.1-bin-hadoop2.3.tgz ]]
+cp spark-1.3.1-bin-hadoop2.3.tgz ..
+cd ..
+tar zxf spark-1.3.1-bin-hadoop2.3.tgz

)

2. it seems when tar fails to decompress the file downloadSpark.sh is not setting a non-0 exit code (or rather the exit code is reset when `rm -f` is called), allowing startSparkCluster.sh to start

Yes, it means process was not killed by `timeout`, but `wget` could drop the connection or something like that. Then it results in un-complete archive.

What I'd like to do as a first step - add exit code check for wget and re-try on that, but this will bring us back to using `-T`. Does it sound as a plan or do you have any other suggestions?

Could be an experiment and if it does not resolve the issue, we can always explore other solutions.

We could certainly try that. I suspect there might be cases where "long time no new packets" are treated as "done" in which there might not be any exit code to check?
Perhaps we should check the download file size, or better against the published hash for each release tar ball?

But in any case the download is bad, retrying could end up with another mirror that is also bad, and this could repeat. This is why I suggested hosting our own copy on s3 or something. I mean, populating the cache shouldn't happen that often, right?

Right, thank you for helping to think it though!

I did a brief glance at wget sources and it looks like the timeout suppose to trigger a special exitcode and can be handled on our side.

Checking the md5 would be a next step, if above does not help.

Hosting our own s3 mirror could be a next one.

Actually that is what Travis CI cache suppose to do.. on the cache population - to check when it happens I have added `ls -la` statement to `before_install` and from what I can tell from the build history now, it looks like different branches\PRs are not really re-using it..
But I will double check that tomorrow and create a PR with the plan above.
